newsitem.title: UK: The Proteus Column - Insurance Stocks.
newsitem.headline: The Proteus Column - Insurance Stocks.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN

This year has been kind to most European and U.S. insurers so far, not only in terms of claims, but also in the form of booming stock markets (with the exception of Tokyo) following the giddy pace set by New York.
Of the 167 insurance stocks monitored by U.S. insurer Cigna, 139 went up in May, 20 went down and four were unchanged.
With their own large portfolios making them quasi investment trusts, insurers are well placed to gain from rising markets.

Good returns on their investment portfolios will help offset falling insurance rates in the non-life sector, while life companies are benefiting from the trend away from state provision for pensions and other social insurance.
Attracting new investors into life insurance products is clearly easier in s rising market.

A glance through price charts shows strong performances in particular from most German, Swiss and Italian insurers. French insurers have been hit by political change and uncertainty over privatisation, but even in France share prices overall hit a new all-time high this week.
In Britain, life insurers have soared in the past 12 months. Non-life share prices are also up, but lag the market as a whole.
As ever, risks are never far away for non-life insurers, and a major catastrophe could quickly knock the gloss of their share prices.
However, at least one potential problem appears not to be a cause for concern for most investors.
The possibility that insurers could be sucked into any global compensation deal now being negotiated in the U.S. with tobacco manufacturers is having little if any impact on insurance stocks
